Data Audit · τ-Trait Released Trajectories

What the released GPT-5 rollouts do and don't tell us

A provenance, setting, reward, and user-behavior validity audit of collinear-ai/tau-trait's published GPT-5 trajectories — 910 rollouts across 4 traits × 4 domains.

Date 2026-08-10 Source tau-trait @ 5855e28 Scope trajectories/gpt5_trajectories/ Artifacts data/intent_eval/tautrait/

The data is usable as a fixed-condition evaluation set, but four things limit what can be claimed from it: trait intensity is not stored in the traces (recoverable only from deleted git files), the neutral baseline covers only 2 of 4 domains, every reward is a single-trial 0/1, and the trait is a latent steer the published trace cannot see — so any validity judgement is measured against the neutral task, not against the trait.

01Data source & provenance

Where the 910 rollouts come from and what is actually in each file.

  • Repo collinear-ai/tau-trait (MIT), companion to arXiv 2510.04491. Released trajectories live in trajectories/gpt5_trajectories/ — 18 JSON files, one per (trait × domain) plus two none baselines.
  • Each file is a list of rollouts; each rollout = {task_id, reward, info, traj, trial}. traj is the agent-side message log (system / user / assistant / tool); assistant tool-calls are preserved with function.name, arguments, and id.
  • info.task carries the neutral user-sim instruction, the ground-truth action sequence (actions), and required outputs (outputs). info.reward_info carries r_actions, r_outputs, gt_data_hash, and the executed actions.
  • No trait metadata is stored in any rollout. The trait label is only in the filename; the intensity and trait_dict that produced it are absent (see §3, Issue I-1).

02Experimental setting

Recovered from run.py, envs/base.py, envs/user.py, and agents/tool_calling_agent.py.

Agent

  • Model: GPT-5 (folder name)
  • Strategy: tool-calling (native function calling)
  • Temperature: 0.0
  • Max steps: 30 (solve(..., max_num_steps=30))
  • System prompt: domain wiki / agent policy

User simulator

  • Model: gpt-4o default, via the Collinear steer endpoint
  • Steer call: temperature=0.7, max_tokens=256
  • Endpoint: steer.collinear.ai/steer_bare
  • Termination: user emits ###STOP###, or terminate_tools, or 30-step cap

Trait injection is latent, not textual. In user.py:113–129 the trait_dict is sent only to the steer endpoint; the non-steer branch ignores it entirely. The user-sim system prompt (build_system_prompt) contains the neutral instruction plus generic rules and never mentions the trait. This is the single most important setting fact for interpreting any text-based audit: the trait is a steering vector applied at generation, invisible in the recorded transcript.

Task set (full test split per domain):

→ 4×4 trait files + 2 none = 910 rollouts. Run params: num_trials=1, seed=10, shuffle=0, tasks in id order.

03Trait intensity — recovered from git history

Not “only low”. Each file sets its named trait to medium, the other three to low.

The released traces do not store the trait_dict. The configs that produced them (eval_scripts/trait_dict_*.json) were removed in commit 2c6b2c9 but survive in git history:

trace filenameconfig (deleted)named traitothers
confusion_*.jsontrait_dict_confusion.jsonconfusion = mediumlow
impatience_*.jsontrait_dict_impatient.jsonimpatience = mediumlow
incoherence_*.jsontrait_dict_coherence.jsonincoherence = mediumlow
skeptical_*.jsontrait_dict_skeptical.jsonskeptical = mediumlow
*_none.json—no trait_dict (null)

Naming mismatch to watch: incoherence_*.json is produced by trait_dict_coherence.json. So each trace is “1 medium + 3 low”, not a clean single-trait condition and not high intensity.

04Reward mechanics

envs/base.py:126 calculate_reward() — a 0/1 outcome score, two gates, no partial credit.

  1. DB-state hash (r_actions). Hash the environment DB after the agent's run; reset, replay the ground-truth action sequence, hash again; reward = 1 only if the two hashes are byte-identical (consistent_hash(to_hashable(self.data))). Any single field differing collapses the whole score to 0.
  2. Output containment (r_outputs). If the task lists required outputs, each must appear as a literal substring (case-insensitive, commas stripped) in some RESPOND_ACTION the agent sent to the user. One missing string → 0.

reward = 1.0 iff both pass. The score is purely terminal-state + required-message; it does not evaluate conversation process, agent style, or how the user behaved. This is why a trait can be flagged “invalid user behavior” while the agent still scores 1 (and vice versa) — the two axes are independent by construction.

05Validity audit — method

A maj@1 offline re-judge with the project's strict user-behavior auditor, run over all 910 rollouts.

  • Judge: scripts/judge_user_intent_preservation.py (4 categories: conversation_structure_violation, premature_termination, ungrounded_reference, missing_constraint). maj@1 — one judge sample per rollout (the project default is maj@3, so variance here is higher).
  • Binding text: the neutral info.task.instruction becomes the “role-play instructions the customer should follow.” The trait is deliberately not passed as persona, because the trait is a latent steer the trace cannot see. So invalid here means: the user behaved in a way no reasonable cooperative customer would, judged against the neutral task — i.e. the trait pushed the user across that line.
  • Pipeline: scripts/persona_opt/judge_tautrait.py converts τ-Trait rollouts to the judge's results.json shape, runs sync maj@1, and aggregates per trait / domain / trait×domain. Outputs in data/intent_eval/tautrait/.

Invalid and hard are decoupled. skeptical|retail is both most-invalid (35%) and hardest (reward 0.192). But incoherence|airline is most-invalid on airline (36.7%) while reward is a middling 0.45, and impatience|retail is noisy-invalid (25.8%) yet easiest-ish (reward 0.583). A trait can be rule-breaking without being effective, and effective without being rule-breaking.

07Issues

Ordered by severity. Severity reflects impact on what can be validly claimed from the released data.

I-1trait_dict not stored in traces — intensity only recoverable from deleted git historycritical · reproducibility

No rollout records the trait_dict or intensity. The producing configs (eval_scripts/trait_dict_*.json) were removed in commit 2c6b2c9 and survive only via git show. Anyone consuming the released JSONs cannot tell from the data itself that the named trait is medium and the rest low; the filename is the only hint, and it is misleading (incoherence ↔ coherence). A re-release should embed trait_dict and user_model in each rollout's info.

I-2single trial released; README reports “averaged across 3 runs”critical · variance

Every rollout has trial = 0 — one sample per (trait, domain, task). The README drop table is “averaged across 3 runs,” so the published trajectories do not reproduce the README numbers and cannot support 3-run-smoothed claims. For telecom (18 tasks) a single trial gives a reward noise band near ±0.1, so cell-level Δ values (e.g. incoherence 0.0 vs impatience −0.111) are not distinguishable from noise.

I-3neutral baseline exists for only 2 of 4 domainscritical · coverage

none files exist only for telecom and telehealth (38 rollouts). Airline and retail have no neutral baseline in the released set, so the trait-vs-neutral drop — the benchmark's headline metric — cannot be computed for half the data from these trajectories alone. Any per-domain “drop” table that includes airline/retail must have come from an unreleased run.

I-4trait is a latent steer; text-based validity is measured against the neutral taskcaveat · measurement

The judge binds the user to the neutral instruction and never sees the trait (it is applied at the steer endpoint, not in text). The auditor's normal rule “persona instructions never ground a violation” therefore cannot apply — we deliberately withheld the trait. So “27% invalid” means trait-driven behavior a strict auditor calls an unreasonable customer against the neutral task, which is exactly the fairness question, but it is not the same as “the user sim failed to follow its trait.” Re-running with the trait supplied as persona would yield a lower, different number.

I-5maj@1 judge variance and the alignment hazard in re-judgingcaveat · method

The audit used maj@1 (project default is maj@3); borderline verdicts flip on a single sample. Additionally, the judge's _select_sims reorders sims by (task_id, trial), and because our first results.json keyed sims by domain|tid (shared across 4 traits), the positional join with per-sim verdicts was initially misaligned — producing absurd cross-domain evidence (a telecom task flagged with telehealth quotes). Fixed by replicating the judge's sort key before joining; any re-use of this pipeline must keep task_id unique per sim or sort-match explicitly.

I-6reward is outcome-only; invalid ≠ hard by constructioncaveat · interpretation

Reward is a DB-hash + output-containment 0/1. A user can break conversational rules yet still let the agent reach the correct terminal state (reward 1), or follow rules yet derail the agent (reward 0). The 27% invalid / 16.8% critical finding and the reward numbers measure orthogonal things and must not be conflated into a single “trait effectiveness” claim.

I-7user-sim cost untracked; steer spend invisibleminor · data gap

info.user_cost is 0.0 for 835 rollouts and null for 75. The steer endpoint's cost is never recorded, so per-rollout and per-trait user-sim spend cannot be audited from the release. Agent cost is also not surfaced in the rollout (only printed at run time).

I-8README references a config file that does not exist in the repominor · docs

The README example command uses notebooks/trait_dict_skeptical.json; the only file present is notebooks/example_trait_dict_skeptical.json (medium + lows). The example is not runnable as printed and slightly misrepresents the eval config used for the released traces.

08Recommendations

  1. Embed provenance in each rollout: add trait_dict, user_model, agent_model, temperature, trial/num_trials to info. This is the single change that fixes I-1, I-2, I-7 at once.
  2. Release the airline/retail none baselines so the headline drop is computable for all four domains from the public set (I-3).
  3. Release multi-trial data (≥3) or explicitly label the release as single-trial and re-state the README table as “from an unreleased 3-run config” (I-2).
  4. For any validity claim, state the measurement frame: “judged against the neutral task, trait withheld” vs “trait supplied as persona.” They answer different questions and give different numbers (I-4).
  5. Re-run the validity audit at maj@3 with per-sim-unique task_ids, and report violation type per cell — the missing_constraint vs structure split is where trait mechanism lives (I-5).
  6. Keep invalid and reward separate in reporting; a combined “trait difficulty” metric needs to be defined deliberately, not assumed (I-6).
Audit run on 2026-08-10. Scripts: scripts/persona_opt/judge_tautrait.py (convert / judge / aggregate). Judge: scripts/judge_user_intent_preservation.py sync mode, model gpt-5.2, maj@1. Full per-rollout verdicts: data/intent_eval/tautrait/per_sim.jsonl; aggregate: tautrait_judge_summary.json.
